predictions.claim_natural: During the first 7 days (Days 1–7), nightly time-in-bed will consistently reach the 7.5-hour target window defined by the 9:00 PM bedtime and 4:30 AM wake time, meaning the wearable will log at least 7.5 hours in bed on each of the 7 nights.

Over the first 14 days (Days 1–14), nightly HRV readings will trend upward toward the 50 ms biomarker target as the fixed 9:00 PM–4:30 AM sleep schedule takes hold and training volume is deliberately reduced in Week 1 with no failure sets, reflecting improving nocturnal recovery across the two-week window.

Daily calorie log entries will show adherence to the 1500 kcal/day target on at least 5 out of every 7 days during the first 14 days, as the structured 11:30am-7:30pm eating window mechanically constrains opportunity to eat outside those hours.

Logged daily protein intake will meet or exceed the 170 g protein floor on at least 5 out of 7 days in the first 14 days, given that hitting 170 g within a 1500 kcal budget requires deliberate high-protein food selection at every meal and the plan explicitly sets this as a non-negotiable floor.

During the first 14 days, all strength training sessions will be logged at reduced volume with no sets taken to failure, consistent with the week-1 ramp discipline rule and the explicit 'no failure sets' restriction that runs through Day 14.

Over the first 14 days, weekly Zone 2 cardio accumulation — governed by RPE rather than a heart-rate device target for this opening period — will trend upward session-over-session as the 5 gym days plus daily ~3-mile walks build toward the 150 min/week Zone 2 target, with total Zone 2 minutes in week 2 exceeding those logged in week 1.

Adherence to the 11:30am–7:30pm eating window will be maintained on at least 6 out of 7 days during the first week, as the structured ramp discipline and reduced-volume Week 1 design lowers the behavioral friction of adopting a new protocol simultaneously with new training demands.

The 9:00 PM bedtime target will be logged as met on at least 5 out of 7 nights in the first 14 days; the fixed 4:30 AM wake time creates a hard backward anchor that makes the 9:00 PM target a concrete, checkable commitment rather than an aspiration, increasing early compliance.

Body weight will trend downward from the 321.6 lb start weight over the first 14 days, driven by the 1500 kcal/day deficit combined with daily ~3-mile walking and 5 gym days/week; a measurable decline on the scale is expected by Day 14.

Daily walking of ~3 miles (roughly 6,000–7,000 steps) will be logged consistently on at least 5 out of every 7 days during the first 14 days, reflecting the plan's mandatory daily movement requirement and the reduced-intensity ramp discipline in Week 1.

Adherence to the 11:30am–7:30pm eating window (an 8-hour daily feeding window) will be maintained on at least 6 out of 7 days in the first week, as logged meal timestamps will consistently fall within that window, reflecting early compliance with the time-restricted eating protocol.

Daily fiber intake logs will show the 25 g minimum fiber target being met on at least 5 out of 7 days during the first two weeks, as the structured 1500 kcal/day nutrition plan with an explicit 25 g fiber floor provides a concrete dietary anchor that supports consistent gut-derived metabolic signaling from the outset.

Resting heart rate (RHR) will trend downward over the first 14 days, consistent with the plan's biomarker target of 55 bpm, as the combination of 7.5-hour sleep (bed 9:00 PM, wake 4:30 AM) and daily Zone 2 walking (~3 miles after work) begins to reduce sympathetic load from Day 1.

HRV will trend upward over the first 14 days toward the plan's biomarker target of 50 ms, driven by the structured sleep schedule (9:00 PM–4:30 AM, 7.5 h nightly) and the deliberately reduced training volume in Week 1 with no failure sets, limiting acute autonomic stress during the adaptation window.

Across the first 7 days of the experiment, the daily calorie log will show at least one deviation from the 1500 kcal target, meaning the within-week coefficient of variation for logged daily intake will be greater than zero — establishing that Day 1–7 intake data cannot be treated as a fixed constant and must be modeled as a distribution rather than a point estimate for any downstream N=1 statistical analysis.

hypotheses.hypothesis: On days when logged calories are at or under the 1500 kcal plan target, next-day weight will be lower than after days over target.
hypotheses.evidence: Pre-registered at genesis from the plan itself: 1500 kcal/day target from a 321.6 lb start (config/user_goals.json); MacroFactor logs daily calories and Withings logs daily weight, so both arms are directly measurable.
hypotheses.confirmation_criteria: Mean next-day weight at least 0.1 lbs lower on adherent days within 30 days, 95% CI excluding 0.
hypotheses.actionable_if_confirmed: Hold the 1,500 kcal baseline through the Foundation phase; escalate only if the trend stalls.

hypotheses.hypothesis: On days reaching roughly 6,000+ steps (the 3-mile daily-movement floor), next-day Whoop recovery will be higher than after low-movement days.
hypotheses.evidence: Pre-registered at genesis from the plan itself: daily movement target '3 miles walking minimum (steps will vary by stride length, roughly 6,000-7,000 steps)' (config/user_goals.json); Apple Health logs steps and Whoop logs recovery daily.
hypotheses.confirmation_criteria: Next-day recovery at least 3 points higher on 6,000+ step days within 30 days, 95% CI excluding 0.
hypotheses.actionable_if_confirmed: Protect the daily walk as a recovery lever, not just an energy-expenditure line.
